correctness.rationale: The criterion for generating kQ/J^2 requires pairwise distinct vertex-label vectors in k^d, surjectivity of each d-dimensional loop arrow-coefficient map, and surjectivity of each nonloop arrow-coefficient map restricted to the codimension-one kernel of the vertex difference covector. Necessity follows from a telescoping coefficient identity for arbitrary words; sufficiency follows by lifting primitive idempotents from the separable quotient and using commutators and diagonal corners. Independent counts of full-rank maps yield all factors. An exhaustive independent algebra-closure checker passes 17 cases (q=2,3,4,5), with GF(4) nonprime field included. Finite tests do not prove uniformity; the proof covers all n,d,q including empty arrow corners.

value.rationale: The precise probability that random elements generate an algebra, not merely existence of generating tuples, is a recognized quantitative invariant. This theorem handles all finite fields, every finite quiver and all generator counts d, yields an exact sharp generator threshold, and establishes a strong nonobvious structural factorization: distinct vertex labels plus independent full-rank conditions on loops and on codimension-one off-diagonal hyperplanes. In particular, nonisomorphic path- and fork-oriented quivers share the same generation distribution. It is a natural complete family-wide enumeration with predictive value, not an arbitrary finite table.
